questions.question: What are Resource Files used for in Robot Framework? (Select all that apply)

options.text: To store reusable keywords
To store variables
To organize imports of other resource files and libraries
To define test cases or tasks
options.explanation: Resource files cannot contain test cases or tasks

questions.question: What is the primary architectural benefit of using resource files in a large test automation project?

options.text: Enables reusability and reduces duplication by centralizing common keywords and variables
Improves test execution speed through parallel processing
options.explanation: Resource files provide organizational benefits, not execution performance improvements

options.text: Automatically generates test documentation from keyword definitions
options.explanation: Documentation generation requires libdoc tool; resource files don't auto-generate docs

options.text: Enforces mandatory code review for all test changes
options.explanation: Resource files are for organization and reuse, not for enforcing development processes

questions.question: How should Resource Files be designed? (Select all that apply)

options.text: To be modular
To be reusable
To be maintainable
To contain all keywords from all parts of the application in one file
options.explanation: Keywords should be grouped by relation, not all in one file

questions.question: What should be the basis for grouping keywords and variables in a resource file? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Common purpose
Common abstraction layer
Common context
Alphabetical order
options.explanation: Grouping should be based on relationship, not alphabetical order

options.text: File size limits
options.explanation: Grouping should be logical, not based on file size

questions.question: Which is a good example of organizing keywords in a resource file?

options.text: All keywords and variables for a specific dialog or part of an application in one file
All keywords that start with the same letter in one file
options.explanation: Grouping should be functional, not alphabetical

options.text: All keywords written by the same person in one file
options.explanation: Grouping should be based on functionality, not authorship

options.text: Random distribution to keep files small
options.explanation: Organization should be logical and purposeful

questions.question: How do you import a resource file?

options.text: Use the Resource setting in *** Settings *** section with the path to the resource file
Use the Library setting in *** Settings *** section
options.explanation: Library is for libraries; Resource is for resource files

options.text: Use the Import setting in *** Settings *** section
options.explanation: The setting is called Resource, not Import

options.text: Resource files are automatically discovered
options.explanation: Resource files must be explicitly imported

questions.question: What file extension should resource files use?

options.text: .resource
.robot (required)
options.explanation: .robot works but .resource is the recommended extension

options.text: .res
options.explanation: .resource is the standard extension

options.text: .rf
options.explanation: .resource is the correct extension

questions.question: When a relative path is given for a resource file import, where is it searched first?

options.text: Relative to the directory where the importing file is located
In the current working directory where robot was executed
options.explanation: It's searched relative to the importing file, not CWD

options.text: In Python's module search path first
options.explanation: Module search path is checked second, after relative location

options.text: In the Robot Framework installation directory
options.explanation: It's searched relative to the importing file first

questions.question: If a resource file is not found relative to the importing file, where is it searched next?

options.text: In directories in Python's module search path
In the current working directory
options.explanation: After relative search, Python's module search path is used

options.text: In the user's home directory
options.explanation: Python's module search path is checked, not home directory

options.text: The import fails immediately
options.explanation: Python's module search path is checked before failing

questions.question: What is the main difference between suite files and resource files regarding sections?

options.text: Resource files do not allow *** Test Cases *** or *** Tasks *** sections
Resource files cannot have *** Settings *** section
options.explanation: Resource files can have *** Settings *** section

options.text: Resource files cannot have *** Keywords *** section
options.explanation: Resource files commonly have *** Keywords *** section

options.text: Resource files use different syntax than suite files
options.explanation: Both use the same syntax; only allowed sections differ

questions.question: Which sections are allowed in resource files? (Select all that apply)

options.text: *** Settings ***
*** Variables ***
*** Keywords ***
*** Comments ***
*** Test Cases ***
options.explanation: Test Cases are not allowed in resource files

options.text: *** Tasks ***
options.explanation: Tasks are not allowed in resource files

questions.question: What is the recommended order of sections in a resource file?

options.text: *** Settings *** → *** Variables *** → *** Keywords *** → *** Comments ***
*** Keywords *** → *** Variables *** → *** Settings *** → *** Comments ***
options.explanation: *** Settings *** should come first

options.text: *** Variables *** → *** Settings *** → *** Keywords *** → *** Comments ***
options.explanation: *** Settings *** should be before *** Variables ***

options.text: The order doesn't matter in resource files
options.explanation: There is a recommended order for consistency

questions.question: What is the *** Settings *** section in resource files used for? (Select all that apply)

options.text: To import libraries
To import other resource files
To provide documentation for the resource file
To define test setup and teardown
options.explanation: Test Setup/Teardown are not available in resource files

questions.question: Which settings are COMMON to both suite files and resource files? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Library - to import libraries
Resource - to import other resource files
Documentation - to provide documentation
Test Setup - to define setup keywords
options.explanation: Test Setup is only in suite files, not resource files

options.text: Suite Setup - to define suite initialization
options.explanation: Suite Setup is only in suite files, not resource files

questions.question: Which setting is available in resource files but NOT commonly used in the same way in suite files?

options.text: Keyword Tags - to set tags for all keywords in the resource file
Test Tags - to set tags for all tests
options.explanation: Test Tags is for suite files, not resource files

options.text: Library - to import libraries
options.explanation: Library is common to both

options.text: Resource - to import resource files
options.explanation: Resource is common to both

questions.question:
Analyze this resource file structure:

```robot
*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary
Resource   common_data.resource
Documentation    Login page keywords and variables

*** Variables ***
${LOGIN_URL}    https://example.com/login
${USERNAME_FIELD}    id=username

*** Keywords ***
Open Login Page
    Open Browser    ${LOGIN_URL}    chrome
    
Enter Credentials
    [Arguments]    ${username}    ${password}
    Input Text    ${USERNAME_FIELD}    ${username}
```

Is this a valid resource file structure?

options.text: Yes, it contains only allowed sections in the correct order
No, it's missing *** Test Cases *** section
options.explanation: Resource files cannot have *** Test Cases ***

options.text: No, *** Keywords *** cannot be in resource files
options.explanation: *** Keywords *** is commonly used in resource files

options.text: No, the sections are in the wrong order
options.explanation: The order is correct: Settings → Variables → Keywords

questions.question: What is the difference between variables defined in suite files vs resource files?

options.text: Variables in resource files can be used outside the file when imported; suite variables are suite-scoped
There is no difference; both work the same way
options.explanation: Resource file variables are accessible to importing files

options.text: Resource file variables are read-only
options.explanation: Both can be modified during execution

options.text: Suite variables are global; resource variables are local
options.explanation: It's the opposite regarding accessibility after import

questions.question: What is the difference between keywords defined in suite files vs resource files?

options.text: Keywords in resource files can be used outside the file when imported; suite keywords are suite-scoped
Suite keywords are faster to execute
options.explanation: Performance is the same; difference is scope

options.text: Resource keywords cannot have arguments
options.explanation: Both can have arguments

options.text: There is no difference in scope
options.explanation: Scope is the key difference

questions.question: Which suite settings are NOT available in resource files? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Suite Setup
Suite Teardown
Test Setup
Test Teardown
Test Tags
Library
options.explanation: Library is available in both suite and resource files

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Documentation setting in a resource file?

options.text: To provide documentation for the resource file itself
To document individual keywords
options.explanation: Keyword documentation uses [Documentation] within the keyword

options.text: To document test cases
options.explanation: Resource files don't contain test cases

options.text: To generate external documentation files
options.explanation: Documentation setting provides content; libdoc generates files

questions.question:
Examine these two files:

```robot
# login_keywords.resource
*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary

*** Keywords ***
Login As Admin
    Login User    admin    admin123

# test_suite.robot
*** Settings ***
Resource    login_keywords.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Admin Test
    Login As Admin
    Open Browser    url    chrome
```

What keywords are available in test_suite.robot? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Login As Admin (from resource file)
SeleniumLibrary keywords (imported in resource file)
BuiltIn library keywords
Only Login As Admin; library imports don't transfer
options.explanation: Library imports in resource files are available to importing suites

questions.question: What happens if a resource file imports another resource file?

options.text: Keywords and variables from both resource files become available to suites importing the first
Only the first resource file's content is available
options.explanation: Imports cascade through resource files

options.text: Circular import error occurs
options.explanation: Cascading imports are allowed and expected

options.text: The nested resource file is ignored
options.explanation: Nested resource files are fully imported

questions.question:
Analyze this structure:

```robot
# common.resource
*** Settings ***
Library    DatabaseLibrary

*** Variables ***
${DB_HOST}    localhost

*** Keywords ***
Connect To DB
    Connect To Database    ${DB_HOST}

# user_keywords.resource  
*** Settings ***
Resource    common.resource

*** Keywords ***
Create User
    Connect To DB
    Execute SQL    INSERT INTO users...

# test.robot
*** Settings ***
Resource    user_keywords.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Test
    Create User
```

What is available in test.robot? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Create User keyword
Connect To DB keyword (from common.resource)
${DB_HOST} variable (from common.resource)
DatabaseLibrary keywords (imported in common.resource)
Only Create User; nested resources don't transfer
options.explanation: All resources in the import chain are available

questions.question: What is the purpose of the *** Comments *** section in resource files?

options.text: To store comments that are ignored and not parsed by Robot Framework
To provide documentation visible in reports
options.explanation: *** Comments *** is ignored; use Documentation for visible docs

options.text: To temporarily disable keywords
options.explanation: While it could be used this way, its purpose is general comments

options.text: To add code review notes that appear in logs
options.explanation: *** Comments *** content is completely ignored

questions.question:
Which file would cause an error?

```robot
A) login.resource
*** Keywords ***
Login User
    # keyword implementation

B) login.resource
*** Test Cases ***
Login Test
    Login User

C) login.resource
*** Settings ***
Library    SeleniumLibrary
*** Variables ***
${URL}    example.com

D) login.resource
*** Comments ***
This is a resource file
```

options.text: B - resource files cannot contain *** Test Cases ***
A - resource files must have *** Settings ***
options.explanation: *** Settings *** is optional in resource files

options.text: C - resource files cannot import libraries
options.explanation: Resource files can import libraries

options.text: D - *** Comments *** is not valid
options.explanation: *** Comments *** is valid in resource files

questions.question: What best practice should guide the organization of keywords in resource files?

options.text: Group related keywords that share a common purpose, abstraction layer, or context
Put all keywords in one resource file for easy access
options.explanation: Keywords should be logically grouped across multiple files

options.text: Organize by keyword name alphabetically
options.explanation: Organization should be functional, not alphabetical

options.text: Create a new resource file for each keyword
options.explanation: Related keywords should be grouped together

questions.question: Consider organizing keywords for an e-commerce application. Which grouping is most appropriate?

options.text: login_keywords.resource, product_catalog_keywords.resource, checkout_keywords.resource
keywords_a_to_m.resource, keywords_n_to_z.resource
options.explanation: Alphabetical grouping is not functional

options.text: all_keywords.resource (single file)
options.explanation: Keywords should be modularly organized

options.text: john_keywords.resource, mary_keywords.resource (by author)
options.explanation: Organize by functionality, not authorship

questions.question: Why is modularity important in resource file design?

options.text: Makes files easier to maintain
Improves reusability across different test suites
Allows importing only needed functionality
Reduces file parsing time significantly
options.explanation: Modularity is for organization, not performance

questions.question:
Compare these import approaches:

```robot
A) Resource    ./keywords/login.resource
B) Resource    C:/project/keywords/login.resource  
C) Resource    login.resource  # login.resource in PYTHONPATH
```

Which approach is most portable?

options.text: C - using PYTHONPATH is most portable and stable
A - relative paths are always most portable
options.explanation: Relative paths are good but PYTHONPATH is more stable across environments

options.text: B - absolute paths guarantee the exact location
options.explanation: Absolute paths are not portable across environments

options.text: All three are equally portable
options.explanation: PYTHONPATH approach is most portable

questions.question:
What happens if you try to execute a resource file directly with the robot command?

```bash
robot login_keywords.resource
```

options.text: No tests/tasks are executed because resource files don't contain them
All keywords in the resource file are executed
options.explanation: Keywords aren't executed without being called from tests

options.text: An error occurs because .resource files cannot be executed
options.explanation: Robot will parse it but find no tests/tasks to run

options.text: The file is automatically converted to a test suite
options.explanation: Resource files remain resource files; they're not converted
